item.title: A Hereditarily Atomic Domain without ACCP
item.description: arXiv:2611.31549v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An integral domain for which every subring is atomic is said to be hereditarily atomic. Every hereditarily atomic cancellative commutative monoid satisfies the ascending chain condition on principal ideals (ACCP), but it remained an open question whether every hereditarily atomic domain satisfies ACCP. We construct a hereditarily atomic domain which does not satisfy ACCP, answering this question in the negative. This domain is an overring of the ring of integer-valued polynomials $Int(\mathbb{Z})$, and its subrings that fail ACCP are precisely those of finite additive index.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Toeniskoetter

item.title: A short proof of Serre positivity
item.description: arXiv:2611.31796v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recently, OpenAI found a proof of the positivity of Serre's intersection multiplicity. The two main ingredients are a descent result on rational $K$-theory with support; and a construction of certain category of asymptotic complexes that identifies with the category of perfect complexes over a connective (non-commutative) derived ring. In this article, we present a simpler proof of Serre positivity that circumvents the second step; instead, we use a ``reduction to the diagonal" trick via the $A_{\text{inf}}$-construction.
item.dc:creator: Linquan Ma

item.title: Spectral and arithmetic classifications of mixed-power difference factor absorbing ideals
item.description: arXiv:2611.32719v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For integers $n\ge2$ and $k\ge1$, a proper ideal $I$ is $(kn,n)$-mixed-power difference factor absorbing if $a^{kn}-b^n\in I$ implies that $a^k-b$ or the complementary geometric-sum factor lies in $I$. Extending the cubic spectral criterion, we classify radical ideals for all exponents via roots of unity in the fraction fields of their minimal-prime quotients, with no finiteness or comaximality assumptions; for radical ideals the condition is independent of $k$. We extend the finite comaximal-prime criterion for quartic pair absorption to all radical ideals and identify its three-component obstruction. Requiring one factor to lie in the radical is equivalent to the radical satisfying the condition for every multiplier, yielding radical descent and extending cubic primary descent. For radical ideals, the condition is equivalent under polynomial and power series extension. Applications include pullbacks of domains and, when the characteristic does not divide $n$, a characterization of geometric integrality of geometrically reduced algebras by stability under field extension; for $n\ge3$, a square-zero extension of such an algebra is stable precisely when the quotient is geometrically integral and the kernel is torsion-free. If the characteristic $p$ divides $n$, the condition depends only on the $p$-part of $n$ and is equivalent to a power-closure condition. We classify square-zero extensions of domains, including nonsplit extensions and idealization ideals with prime projection. For homogeneous idealizations over $P$-primary bases with $2\notin P$, a related quartic criterion
item.dc:creator: Omar H. Taha, Akram Salim, Hwankoo Kim

item.title: Max-degree filtration, Koszul complexes, and Multicolor Permutation Wordle
item.description: arXiv:2611.33113v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We explore the Koszul resolutions of a family of ideals, each generated by multivariate polynomials that split completely into linear factors. The motivating examples come from the game Permutation Wordle of Kutin and Smithline, as analyzed by Kutin, Smithline, and Vatter, and an open question, Conjecture 4.5 in Kutin and Smithline's work on Multicolor Permutation Wordle. For each ideal in this family, with our chosen generators, the Koszul differentials are strict for the max-degree filtration and, more generally, at every multidegree whose coordinates form a set of consecutive integers. The resulting dimension count resolves Kutin and Smithline's conjecture. The proof is an induction in which each inductive step is an iteration. The core argument is human generated. The present proof, developed with AI assistance, separates the iteration of multidegree reductions from the mapping cone induction. This method avoids the need to chase compatibility of lifts up to the top grade of the complex.
item.dc:creator: Lawren M. Smithline

item.title: Around the base ideal and the base locus of a Keller map
item.description: arXiv:2611.29705v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\varphi_F:\Bbbk^n\to\Bbbk^n$ be a Keller map defined by $n$ polynomials $F_1,\ldots,F_n$ in $n$ indeterminates $X=X_1,\ldots,X_n$ over a field $\Bbbk$ of characteristic zero. Miranda-Neto defined the base ideal of $\varphi_F$ as the ideal $I_F$ generated by $F_1,\ldots,F_n$ and the base locus of $\varphi_F$ as the affine algebraic set $V_F=V(I_F)$ determined by the ideal $I_F$. He proved that $I_F$ is a radical ideal, which is a finite intersection of $v_F$ maximal ideals, where ${\rm card}(V_F)\leq v_F$, understanding that $v_F=0$, when $I_F$ is improper. In this paper, we first prove that $v_F\leq \dim_{\Bbbk}(\Bbbk[X]/I_F)\leq [\Bbbk(X):\Bbbk(F)]$. Using invertible affine transformations on the recent counterexample to the Jacobian Conjecture announced by Alp\"oge, we show that $I_F$ might indeed be improper and that the following cases, $0<{\rm card}(V_F)=v_F<[\Bbbk(X):\Bbbk(F)]$, $0<{\rm card}(V_F)=v_F=[\Bbbk(X):\Bbbk(F)]$, $0<{\rm card}(V_F)<v_F<[\Bbbk(X):\Bbbk(F)]$ and $0={\rm card}(V_F)<v_F<[\Bbbk(X):\Bbbk(F)]$ might occur. We finish by giving a purely topological equivalent reformulation of the Jacobian Conjecture in terms of the irreducibility of $V_F$.
item.dc:creator: Bartomeu Enrich Lucas, Francesc Planas-Vilanova

item.title: Simultaneous Waring problems for binary forms and the geometry of rational curves
item.description: arXiv:2611.32267v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the simultaneous Waring problem for binary forms and its geometric applications to rational curves. By analyzing the minimal free resolution of the simultaneous annihilator, we establish formulas for both simultaneous Waring ranks and border Waring ranks including explicit computations for binary monomials. As a geometric application, we explicitly describe parametrizations of rational curves up to projective equivalence. We determine the minimum dimension of a rational normal scroll containing the curve as a section of its ruling in terms of the minimal generators of the corresponding simultaneous annihilator. For rational curves lying as divisors on rational normal surface scrolls, we characterize their smoothness and describe the generators of their defining ideals.
item.dc:creator: Maciej Ga{\l}\k{a}zka, Jaewoo Jung, Hyunsuk Moon

item.title: On the solving degree and complexity of Gr\"obner Basis computation over finite fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.32456v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Solving systems of multivariate polynomial equations over finite fields is a central problem in algebraic cryptanalysis, commonly approached using Gr\"obner basis algorithms. The complexity of Gr\"obner basis computation depends on the algorithm employed and is governed by the solving degree, defined as the maximum degree of the polynomials processed during the computation. Estimating this quantity is therefore crucial, and several bounds in terms of the degree of regularity have been established in the literature. In this work, we investigate the effect of Buchberger's criteria on the elimination of redundant pairs, and prove that the solving degree of a Gr\"obner basis algorithm combining linear algebra with Buchberger's original algorithm is bounded above by the degree of regularity defined by the leading forms of the involved polynomials. This result provides a rigorous justification for using the degree of regularity in complexity estimates for Gr\"obner basis algorithms, thereby supporting a common assumption in algebraic cryptanalysis. We refine the complexity analysis by establishing bounds on the number of pairs that must be processed. These bounds improve upon published complexity estimates, with particularly significant gains in certain parameter ranges.
item.dc:creator: Irene Di Muzio, Igor Semaev

item.title: Theta Functions and Intrinsic Mirrors of Laurent Phenomenon Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.32571v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct bases of upper Laurent phenomenon algebras over a field by minimizing Newton polytopes in a single seed. For any translation-invariant total order on the exponents, each least exponent $a$ that occurs determines a smallest Newton polytope $Q_a$. Choose one element with Newton polytope $Q_a$ and least term $x^a$ for each such $a$. These elements form a basis. In every reachable seed chart, every Gauss valuation takes a nonzero basis expansion to the minimum of its values on the nonzero summands. Suppose the algebra has Laurent coefficients and smooth spectrum over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. After setting the curve parameters to one, we compute theta products on the intrinsic mirror from the exchange polynomials and give a finite presentation of the mirror algebra. A seed has a polynomial corner if each exchange polynomial can be multiplied by a unit of the coefficient ring to give a polynomial with constant term one. At such a corner, order the exponents by a weight with strictly positive, rationally independent coordinates. For every lattice exponent $a$ and integral weight $p$, the theta function indexed by $p$ has least $a$-weight $\min_{b\in Q_a}\langle b,p\rangle$ in the corresponding mirror chart. This reciprocity holds for cyclic exchanges and arbitrary pole orders. For fixed exchange supports and constant terms one, we determine when the mirror is smooth and the second mirror recovers the original algebra in the chosen torus coordinates. The coefficient tuples for which both conditions hold form a computable finite set. All their entries are positive integers.
item.dc:creator: Jiarui Fei

item.title: Undershoot of h-fold sumsets: Ap\'ery spectra, similar ordering and the three-distance theorem
item.description: arXiv:2611.33046v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a finite set $A_0\subset\mathbb{N}$ with $0\in A_0$, $\max A_0=d$ and $\gcd(A_0)=1$, and a target $T$, the undershoot at level $h$ is the distance from $T$ down to the largest element of the $h$-fold sumset $hA_0$ not above $T$. Its total over $T\in[0,hd]$ is bounded in $h$: for large $h$ it equals the sum of the masses of two numerical semigroups attached to $A_0$, where the mass adds $L(L+1)/2$ over the maximal runs of $L$ gaps. We describe how the total reaches this limit: it can rise to it, fall to it, or climb past it and return. When the monomial curve of $A_0$ is arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay, two Ap\'ery sets give every undershoot exactly, and partial sums of a fixed spectrum bound the total from below, with equality at every level exactly when two threshold sequences are similarly ordered; the total then rises concavely to its limit, reached exactly at the sumsets regularity. We characterize the similarly ordered four-element sets. For $\{0,a,b,2b\}$ with $0<a<b$ coprime, the three-distance theorem gives the total in explicit quadratic pieces. A non-Cohen-Macaulay set exceeds its limit at every failing level $h$ with $hd$ at least the sum of the two conductors; every such four-element set does so, and a five-element example never does. For arbitrary sets, finite corner data give the exact undershoot over any window.
item.dc:creator: Prashant Chaudhary, Kapil Khandelwal

item.title: Infinitely many associated primes of local cohomology modules of ramified regular local rings
item.description: arXiv:2604.10964v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct examples of local cohomology modules of ramified regular local rings with infinitely many associated primes and infinite Bass numbers.
item.dc:creator: Linquan Ma

item.title: Counterexamples to Peskine-Szpiro's conjectures on modules of finite projective dimension
item.description: arXiv:2608.24018v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give counterexamples to the remaining homological conjectures of Peskine-Szpiro concerning modules of finite projective dimension over Noetherian local rings. Specifically, we show that the dimension inequality, the strong intersection conjecture, and the grade conjecture are all false in general.
item.dc:creator: Linquan Ma

item.title: Local cohomology module with infinitely many associated primes over ramified regular local rings of the least possible dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.26655v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In \cite{Ma} we have observed the example of local cohomology module with infinitely many associated primes over a 12 dimensional ramified regular local ring. In this paper we construct examples of local cohomology modules with infinitely many associated primes over ramified regular local rings of two different ring dimensions. The result of this paper is very much dependent on the result (\cite{SS}, Theorem 2.6).
item.dc:creator: Rajsekhar Bhattacharyya

item.title: A Higgs category for the cluster variety of triples of flags
item.description: arXiv:2509.04863v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The cluster variety of triples of flags (associated with a split simple Lie group of Dynkin type Delta) plays a key role in higher Teichmuller theory as developed by Fock-Goncharov, Jiarui Fei, Ian Le, ... and Goncharov-Shen. We refer to it as the basic triangle associated with Delta. In this paper, for simply laced Delta, we construct and study a Higgs category (in the sense of Yilin Wu) which we expect to categorify the basic triangle. This category is a certain exact dg category (in the sense of Xiaofa Chen) which is Frobenius and stably 2-Calabi-Yau. We show that it has indeed the expected cyclic group symmetry and that its derived category has the expected braid group symmetry. A key ingredient in our construction is a conjecture by Merlin Christ, whose proof occupies most of this paper. The proof is based on a new description of the Higgs category in terms of Gorenstein projective dg modules. Our techniques are in the spirit of Orlov in his work on triangulated categories of graded B-branes.
item.dc:creator: Bernhard Keller, Miantao Liu

item.title: Parke-Taylor Varieties
item.description: arXiv:2509.09323v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Parke--Taylor functions are certain rational functions on the Grassmannian of lines encoding MHV amplitudes in particle physics. For $n$ particles there are $n!$ Parke--Taylor functions, corresponding to all orderings of the particles. Linear relations between these functions have been extensively studied in the last years. We here describe all non-linear polynomial relations between these functions in a simple combinatorial way and study the variety parametrized by them, called the Parke--Taylor variety. We show that the Parke--Taylor variety is equal to the log canonical embedding of the moduli space $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0,n}$ into $\mathbb{P}^{(n-2)!-1}$ due to Keel and Tevelev by exhibiting a concrete linear isomorphism with the realization in coordinates based on Kapranov's map. We also show that the intersection with the algebraic torus recovers the open part, $\mathcal{M}_{0,n}$. We give an explicit description of this isomorphism. Unlike the realization of the log canonical embedding by using the iterated Kapranov's map, this Parke--Taylor embedding very explicitly respects the symmetry of the $n$ marked points and is constructed in a single-step procedure, avoiding the intermediate embedding into a product of projective spaces.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Hollering, Dmitrii Pavlov

item.title: A nine-line counterexample to a conjecture on the minimal degree of Jacobian relations
item.description: arXiv:2607.01985v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct two arrangements of nine lines in the complex projective plane with isomorphic intersection lattices, of weak combinatorics $(n_2,n_3,n_4)=(9,7,1)$, whose defining equations $f$ and $g$ satisfy $${\rm mdr}(f)=4,\qquad {\rm mdr}(g)=5.$$ Since $4<9/2$, this disproves a conjecture of the first author which would have implied Terao's Conjecture on the combinatorial nature of the freeness of line arrangements. Equivalently, the rank two vector bundle of logarithmic vector fields is strictly semistable for the first arrangement and stable for the second one. Hence the stability of this bundle is not determined by the intersection lattice, which gives a counterexample to a conjecture of Abe. The two arrangements also have different minimal free resolutions of their Milnor algebras. All computations are exact, and a short SINGULAR script performing them is included.
item.dc:creator: Alexandru Dimca, Piotr Pokora

item.title: Hilbert functions over the exterior algebra and f-vectors in higher rank I: Amata-Crupi monomial modules, Kozlov polytopes, and r-vectors of simplicial complexes
item.description: arXiv:2609.23605v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $E$ be the exterior algebra on $n$ generators over a field, and let $F$ be a graded free $E$-module with $r$ generators, of degrees $d_1 \le \dots \le d_r$. We determine the convex hull of the set of Hilbert functions of the quotients $F/M$, where $M$ runs over the monomial submodules of Amata and Crupi. The hull is the Minkowski sum of $r$ shifted copies of one and the same simplex: the Kozlov simplex, which Kozlov proved in 1997 to be the convex hull of the $f$-vectors of simplicial complexes on $n$ vertices. For $r=1$ the statement is Kozlov's theorem, so this is a rank-$r$ generalization of it. We give a self-contained proof, including a proof of Kozlov's theorem from the local Lubell-Yamamoto-Meshalkin inequality, which is in essence Kozlov's own second proof, and the facet description of the Kozlov simplex that this proof contains. Along the way we isolate the class of submodules for which the argument works, the ideal-direct-sum modules, and show by example that the Hilbert function of a graded submodule outside that class need not be a shifted sum of $f$-vectors at all. The combinatorial content is stated separately, in language that uses no algebra, as a result on $r$-vectors of simplicial complexes and their $ff$-vectors. Finally we determine the vertices of the Minkowski sum at rank two: which sums of vertices of the summands survive as vertices. The facet descriptions at rank two, conjectured in the first version of this paper, and the vertex and facet descriptions at every rank are proved in Part IV of this series.
item.dc:creator: Jan Snellman

item.title: Non-vanishing of the structure-sheaf cohomology of affine henselian schemes and henselian affinoids
item.description: arXiv:2609.30851v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian pair such that $A$ is a domain of characteristic zero and $I\ne0$. We prove that any flat affine henselian scheme of finite presentation over $(A,I)$ has nonzero first structure-sheaf cohomology whenever one of its fibers over a point in $V(I)$ has positive dimension. This in particular gives a negative answer to the question by Devadas in the mixed-characteristic case. As an application, we also prove that the first structure-sheaf cohomology does not vanish for henselian affinoids of positive dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Yoshinori Gongyo, Fumiharu Kato, Takayuki Uchiba

item.title: An explicit tame factorization of the four-variable Anick automorphism
item.description: arXiv:2610.11013v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\delta=xz-yt$. We give an explicit tame factorization of the Anick automorphism $$ f=(x+\delta t,y+\delta z,z,t) $$ of $F[x,y,z,t]$. After a linear change of coordinates, the factorization consists of sixteen elementary automorphisms, all fixing $z$. The proof uses a commutator construction with variables already present in the algebra. A complete list of the elementary factors is included in Section 5. The explicit polynomial factorization identities are defined over $Z[1/2]$; no conclusion in characteristic $2$ is asserted. We also prove that the Freudenburg--Moser-Jauslin involution $$ \tau(a,b,x,y)= \bigl(b,a,-b^3x+(1+ab+a^2b^2)y,(1-ab)x+a^3y\bigr). $$ of $F[a,b,x,y]$ is tame over every field of characteristic different from $2$ and $3$, and list an explicit factorization in Appendix.
item.dc:creator: Alexei Miasnikov, Ivan Shestakov
